name: Hardware-Accelerated Simulated Radiography (Non-Emissive)
definition: A volume rendering technique for non-emissive objects that accumulates attenuation coefficients in a floating-point off-screen P-buffer, using hardware-accelerated rasterization of geometric cells (hexahedra or tetrahedra) to simulate X-ray radiography.
summary: Hardware-Accelerated Simulated Radiography is a GPU technique for non-emissive objects that simulates X-rays by iteratively rendering unsorted, overlapping geometric cells into a P-buffer to minimize synchronization overhead.
